policy: Entries waive one package + one GHSA advisory id each. A new advisory on an allowlisted package is NOT inherited and fails the gate. build-dev-toolchain entries are accepted without an expiry only while the vulnerable code never ships; runtime-accepted-debt entries MUST carry a rationale, an expiry, and a tracked follow-up in .agent/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, and are the explicit escalation path when no compatible fix exists. Never silently waived.

allowlist.rationale: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements (high, CWE-347; advisory range is every node-forge release, so no in-range patch exists and npm audit only offers an expo@44 major downgrade). Reachability re-verified 2026-10-02: the only path is expo@57.0.24 -> @expo/cli@57.0.26 -> node-forge@1.4.0 and @expo/code-signing-certificates@0.0.6 (Expo CLI update code-signing certificate parsing, a prebuild/CLI step on the developer/CI machine). Zero first-party imports of node-forge in apps/mobile/src; zero node-forge/pki/pkcs signatures in the exported web bundle (the only 'forge' substring in dist is a word-game distractor list); expo-updates is not a dependency, so no runtime manifest signature verification exists in the shipped app. The vulnerable verification code never ships.
allowlist.tracking: .agent/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT.md -> 2026-10-02 node-forge toolchain review (post-067 terminal certification campaign)

allowlist.rationale: ICNS parser infinite loop reached only while Metro parses images on the developer/CI machine; the vulnerable code never ships in the app bundle (no runtime import path). Tracked in .agent/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT.md.
JXL/HEIF parser infinite loops with the same Metro-only reachability as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr; build-time image parsing only, not embedded in the shipped binary.

v3/v5/v6 buffer-bounds advisory for uuid < 11.1.1 reached only through xcode -> @expo/config-plugins -> Expo CLI/prebuild/config toolchain. The vulnerable call pattern (explicit buf argument) is not exercised by first-party code or the toolchain; not runtime-bundled.

Quadratic-time expansion of the `{a},b}` rewrite (moderate). Reachability re-verified 2026-09-30 with `npm ls brace-expansion --omit=dev`: every path is expo-router@57.0.22 -> @testing-library/react-native@14.0.1 -> jest@29.7.0 -> @jest/core -> glob@7.2.3 -> minimatch@3.1.5 -> brace-expansion@1.1.18 (test/Metro glob expansion only), plus @expo/fingerprint@0.20.13 -> minimatch@10.2.6 -> brace-expansion@5.0.9 (Expo CLI fingerprint step). No first-party source imports glob/minimatch/brace-expansion; the vulnerable parser never ships in the app bundle. Accepted while `glob@7` / `minimatch@3` are pulled in transitively by the test harness.

Uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups causing stack exhaustion (high). Same toolchain-only reachability as GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr: jest/@jest/core -> glob@7.2.3 -> minimatch@3.1.5 -> brace-expansion@1.1.18, exercised only by Jest's own module/test glob expansion on the developer/CI machine. No runtime import path; not bundled. Accepted while `glob@7` / `minimatch@3` are transitive dependencies of the pinned Jest 29 toolchain.

Uncontrolled recursion in parseCommaParts causing stack exhaustion (high). Same toolchain-only reachability as the two sibling brace-expansion advisories: brace-expansion@1.1.18 via jest/@jest/core -> glob@7.2.3 -> minimatch@3.1.5, and brace-expansion@5.0.9 via expo@57.0.24 -> @expo/fingerprint@0.20.13 -> minimatch@10.2.6 (Expo CLI fingerprinting). Neither parser is reachable from first-party runtime code; the vulnerable code never ships.

Stack-exhaustion DoS on deeply nested patterns (high; advisory range <=3.0.3 equals the latest published braces release, so no fixed version exists and npm audit's only offered fix is a jest@30 semver-major upgrade). Reachability reproduced 2026-10-07 with `npm ls braces --omit=dev`: the production path is expo@57.0.24 -> @expo/cli@57.0.26 -> @expo/metro-file-map@57.0.3 -> micromatch@4.0.8 -> braces@3.0.3, i.e. Metro's file-map pattern expansion running on the developer/CI build machine; the second path is the Jest 29 test harness (@jest/core -> micromatch -> braces). Zero first-party imports of braces/micromatch in apps/mobile/src or scripts; the vulnerable parser has no runtime import path and never ships in the app bundle. By contrast, the separate CRITICAL shell-quote advisory found in the same audit was genuinely remediated in this pass (lockfile update to shell-quote@1.12.0); only this entry needed acceptance because no upstream fix exists. Exit condition: drop when metro/metro-file-map stops depending on the vulnerable braces line (upstream braces release or the next Expo/Metro upgrade) or when npm offers a non-major fixed resolution; review at the next Expo SDK upgrade.

DoS through unbounded precision specifiers (moderate; advisory range <=1.1.3 equals the latest published sprintf-js release, so no fixed version exists and npm audit's only offered fix is a jest@30 semver-major upgrade). Reachability reproduced 2026-10-07 with `npm ls sprintf-js --omit=dev`: the only production path is react-native@0.86.3 -> @react-native/jest-preset@0.86.3 -> babel-jest@29.7.0 -> babel-plugin-istanbul@6.1.1 -> @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config -> js-yaml@3.15.2 -> argparse@1.0.10 -> sprintf-js@1.0.3, i.e. coverage-config loading inside the test-toolchain (babel-plugin-istanbul is exercised only when Jest coverage is enabled on the developer/CI machine). Zero first-party imports of sprintf-js/argparse/js-yaml in apps/mobile/src or scripts; the vulnerable formatter has no runtime import path and never ships in the app bundle. Exit condition: drop when the shipped jest-expo/istanbul chain no longer resolves the vulnerable sprintf-js line (upstream release or the next Expo/Jest toolchain upgrade); review at the next Expo SDK upgrade.

ReDoS (exponential decoding of malformed percent-encoded input, CWE-400/405/407) reached at runtime via expo-router@57 -> query-string@7.1.3 -> decode-uri-component. Impact is a crafted deep-link query string hanging the JS thread. Campaign 053 re-evaluated the officially compatible remediation envelope: expo-router@57.0.22 (current SDK 57 line, latest 57.x) pins query-string ^7.1.3, and every query-string 7.x release pins decode-uri-component ^0.2.2, so no patch within the supported line can carry the fix; query-string@9.x would supply the patched decode-uri-component@^0.5.0 but 0.5.0 is `"type": "module"` (ESM-only) while expo-router requires query-string from CommonJS (`__importStar(require("query-string"))` in build/getPathFromState.js), so forcing it would break route parsing at runtime; npm audit's only offered fix remains an expo-router semver-major downgrade to 5.1.11, which is out of scope and would regress SDK 57. App-owned route parameters are additionally bounded by `apps/mobile/src/routing/route-params.ts`, which is defense in depth only and does NOT remediate this upstream decoder advisory. Follow-up: drop this entry when expo-router advances to a query-string major that carries the fix (next planned Expo SDK upgrade); tracked in .agent/KNOWN_ISSUES.md.
